entries.name: 3/4 Sit-Up
entries.reason: Redrawn on 9 October 2026 at the owner's request, from the description accepted that day: the earlier drawing lifted the trunk as one stiff piece and did not show the three-quarter lowering. Source-bound side-view draft with a spine that curls: lying with the knees bent and the feet held down, hands by the head; the trunk curls and sits up until it is upright, lowers only three quarters of the way so the shoulders stop short of the floor, sits up again from there, and lies back only at the end of the set. The hips and feet do not move.
entries.summary: With the feet secured, sit up until the torso is upright, lower only three quarters of the way so the shoulders stay off the floor, and start the next repetition from there.

frames.caption: Lie on your back on the floor with the knees bent and the feet secured, hands resting lightly behind or beside your head.
Bending at the hips and spine, sit up until the torso is upright.
Lower under control only three quarters of the way back down, so the shoulders stop short of the floor.
Start each following repetition from there. Sit up until the torso is upright.
Lower three quarters, no further.
The shoulders return to the floor only at the end of the set.
Hands light; do not pull on the head.

entries.name: Cable Seated Crunch
entries.reason: Redrawn on 8 October 2026 at the owner's request, because the earlier drawing contradicted this text: it showed the athlete lying on the floor. Source-bound side-view draft with a spine that curls: sitting on a flat bench with the back to a high pulley, rope ends over the shoulders at the upper chest; the hips and legs do not move while the spine curls the trunk forward and the elbows travel toward the hips, a pause, and a slower return to sitting tall. The cable runs over the shoulder and only lengthens on the way down.
entries.summary: Sitting on a bench with your back to a high pulley and the rope at the upper chest, curl the torso forward with the hips still, pause, then return slowly to sitting tall.

frames.caption: Sit on a flat bench with your back to a high pulley and hold the rope ends over the shoulders against the upper chest.
Keeping the hips still, curl the torso forward so the elbows travel toward the hips.
Pause. Curl the ribs toward the hips.
Return slowly to sitting tall, against the cable.
Hips stay still.

entries.name: Jackknife Sit-Up
entries.reason: Own drawn frames: the legs lift (the knees and feet rise together, the bones holding) while the hands reach toward the feet - the folding tell an athlete sees at a glance. Full notes and open questions in the daily review.
entries.summary: Six drawn positions of a jackknife sit-up folding hands to f

frames.caption: Lie back with the arms reaching overhead and the legs long.
Lift the legs and curl the trunk toward one another.
Reach the hands toward the feet at the top.
Pause with the trunk and the legs folded together.
Open both ends again without momentum.
Return long and set the pelvis for the next rep.

entries.name: Janda Sit-Up
entries.reason: Redrawn on 8 October 2026 at the owner's request, because the earlier drawing contradicted this text: it showed straight legs. Source-bound side-view draft with a spine that curls: knees bent to a right angle with the feet flat and the arms at the sides; the trunk peels off the floor and curls up over three and a half seconds, and lowers the same way over the same time. Not drawn: the glutes and hamstrings held tight, which is the point of the movement and which a figure cannot show; the captions carry it.
entries.summary: Knees bent to ninety degrees and feet flat, hold the glutes and hamstrings tight and curl the trunk up over a slow count, then lower over a matching count.

frames.caption: Lie on your back with the knees bent to about ninety degrees and the feet flat on the floor, arms resting at your sides.
Tighten the glutes and hamstrings hard, hold that tension, and curl the trunk up over a slow three to six second count.
Hold that tension for the whole rep.
Lower back down under the same tension across a matching count.
Take the descent as slowly as the climb.
